companions.name: M4 V66 B
companions.description: The secondary star of the eclipsing binary M4 V66, 0.7443 solar masses and 0.8298 solar radii; the two stars eclipse each other every 8.111 days.

radius.source: Secondary radius (solar radii) 0.8298 +/- 0.0053, as DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164) lists it from Kaluzny et al. (2013AJ....145...43K)

mass.source: Secondary mass (solar masses) 0.7443 +/- 0.0042, as DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164) lists it from Kaluzny et al. (2013AJ....145...43K)

temperature.source: Secondary log Teff 3.774 +/- 0.008, as DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164) lists it from Kaluzny et al. (2013AJ....145...43K): 5943 K

orbit.source: M4 V66: P 8.11130346 d and primary-eclipse time HJD 2449900.41965 (Section II, Equations (1)); i 89.444 degrees (Table 11 (Photometric parameters), columns V65 | V66 | V69); e 0.0 (circular). HJD is taken as BJD_TDB (under a minute apart); at the primary eclipse the secondary is in front, the component these papers call primary being the one eclipsed at phase 0. Separation from Kepler's third law with DEBCat's masses

text.card: The secondary star of M4 V66, a pair that eclipse each other every 8.111 days.
text.introduction: It has 0.7443 solar masses and 0.8298 solar radii; its partner has 0.7842 and 0.9347, measured from the eclipses and the stars' motions.
text.locator: DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164), M4 V66: Mass, Radius and Period, from Kaluzny et al. (2013AJ....145...43K)
